_comment: Exploratory sweep, NOT a scoring run. n=1 per cell, so every number here is directional only. Its purpose was to find which questions separate the arms at all before spending the full matrix - and it changed the design.
harness: Claude Code subagents (.claude/agents/eval-*.md), one question per agent, answers scored by hand

models.exceptions: benchmark-trap also run on sonnet and opus

caveats: One run per cell. No repeats, so nothing here survives a significance test.
Correctness scored by hand against ground_truth, not by a judge.
Tool calls are self-reported by the agent under test.
The words arm was only run on four questions.

findings.1_alerts_and_schema_work_prose_does_not: Every question the rich arm won, it won on a computed ALERT or a SCHEMA field. On the two where rich had only INTERPRETATION prose (overheating, benchmark-trap) it failed exactly like thin - rich-Haiku read '>1.5 = significant overheating', saw 3.59, and answered 'very low'. The words arm makes this unambiguous: on building-size and total-vs-per-m2 it produced answers IDENTICAL to thin while carrying the full prose.
findings.2_this_inverts_the_design_note: The note frames A->B (words) as the thing to prove and 'most of the build'. At Haiku, A->B buys almost nothing and B->C buys all of it. The defensible message is not 'write better descriptions' but 'compute the answer server-side'.
findings.3_binary_verdict_questions_saturate: invented-label, metered-vs-model, human-typing and heat-pump were all answered correctly by the thin arm. Their answers are visible in the payload (labelCount 0) or guessable from adjacent signals (A+ label implies heat-pump suitability). A question separates only when the answer needs a value, constant or convention that is NOT in the payload.
findings.4_separation_can_collapse_as_the_model_i: gas-estimate separated at Haiku (thin 140 vs rich 253) but thin-Sonnet reached 250-300 by another route (EP-2 fossil, 9.77 kWh/m3). Read every separation as model-specific until shown otherwise.
findings.5_one_clean_confirmation_of_the_thesis: On gas-estimate, rich-Haiku (253) matched thin-Sonnet (250-300) while thin-Haiku failed (140). The layer bought exactly one model tier on that question.
findings.6_call_count_is_a_dead_metric: get_building_profile is one-shot, so nearly every run was 1 call. The only 2-call runs were compensating searches into get_weather_context when the payload did not resolve the question - thin on heat-pump, and rich on overheating where it spent the extra call confirming a wrong answer. FABRICATION discriminates where call count does not: invented fossil shares, invented units, invented thresholds.
findings.7_the_prose_can_be_wrong_too: human-typing assumed a postcode with a space must be normalised. PDOK accepts it, so the thin arm passed '3543 AR' straight through and succeeded. The question tested nothing.
findings.8_the_ladder_on_wrong_unit: wrong-unit gives the strongest single result in the set: thin-Haiku answers 105 m2 (confidently wrong), thin-Opus correctly refuses because the schema has no huisletter parameter, and rich-Haiku answers 92 m2. rich-Haiku STRICTLY BEATS thin-Opus. It also shows the layer does two different things: it makes the weak model right, and the strong model safe.
findings.9_prose_only_questions_are_a_model_cliff: overheating and benchmark-trap are the two questions whose rule lives only in INTERPRETATION prose. Both behave identically across every cell: Haiku fails on BOTH arms, Opus passes on BOTH. Two questions, eight cells, same pattern. The arm is irrelevant when the knowledge is prose.
findings.10_class_E_not_found: No question was found where the rich arm fails at Opus. Within this set there is no evidence of a gap that the layer plus a strong model cannot close. Worth saying out loud rather than leaving as an absence.
